alt_text: AI-generated artistic interpretation of El Paular monastery at night, with the late-Gothic atrium, a brick-and-stone bell tower whose spire is gone, and a low octagonal chapel in the Lozoya valley.
description: From the valley approach at night, El Paular is defined by Juan Guas’s late-Gothic church atrium and a brick-and-stone bell tower left flat-topped after the 1903 spire was lost. The Baroque Transparente reads as a low octagonal chapel volume. There is no conical turret and no cluster of exterior domes. The Guadarrama rises behind the poplars.
